findings.title: Shell-wall cutaway uses the wall's centre, so near a room corner the back wall never folds away and hides Pip, the held item and the target completely (Meeting spawn, Spectrum storeroom)
findings.problem: The cutaway in src/game.ts:385 decides whether a shell wall drops to its 0.9 m stub from `wall.normal.dot(toCam)>.2`, where toCam is the normalised direction from the wall group's origin, which is the wall's centre (src/levels/decor.ts:33, shellWall places the group at x=0 for the 33 m back wall), to the camera. When Pip stands near one end of a long wall, such as the Meeting spawn at (-10,-5.8) next to the server closet or the Spectrum storeroom door at (-10.1,-4.4), and the player orbits behind the back wall, the camera is outside the room. But seen from the wall's centre 10 m away, the camera lies mostly sideways (Meeting y180: cam (-10.9,3.7,-12), dot about 0.18 < 0.2). So the wall stays full height (`shell scales 1,1`). The full 3 m wall then fills about 75% of the frame. Pip, the power strip (step 1 target) and, in Spectrum, the carried pod, the pad and the objective marker all disappear. Nothing fades, because shell walls are not occluders and the occluder ray only tests `this.occluders`. The clean route starts in exactly these corners (Meeting reel closet and spawn; Spectrum storeroom). This is the 'camera hides the player/objective' complaint the design rules exist to prevent. It is separate from the known 'only pillars fade' issue (DR-12 Known): here the dedicated cutaway system exists but misfires because of a geometry error. It also explains part of the DR-75 'low lips' behaviour.
evidence: src/game.ts:385 (toCam from wall.group.parent world position = wall centre; stub only if dot>.2)
src/levels/decor.ts:32-40,73 (only back and left shell walls; group origin at wall centre)
mockups/review5/shots/snap-grab-target-60-mt-spawn-z9-y180.jpg (Meeting spawn, zoom 9, yaw +180°: frame is a blank wall, Pip invisible)
mockups/review5/shots/snap-grab-target-s-pad-z9-y180.jpg (Spectrum, holding pod at storeroom: wall corner fills frame, Pip/pod/pad/marker hidden)
s9 log: MEETING spawn z9 y180 strip:HID(h1.94) pip:HID(h1.94); occl y180 feet/chest/head all blocked by non-occluder op1 mesh bbTop 3 at z≈-10; SPECTRUM pad z9 y135/y180 marker:HID(h1.94)
findings.fix: In src/game.ts:385 replace the centre-direction test with the camera's signed distance to the wall plane, and gate it on Pip being inside: `const out=wall.normal.dot(new T.Vector3(cam.position.x-at.x,0,cam.position.z-at.z)); const stub=out>0.3;` (the camera is on the wall's outer side, whatever its lateral offset). Optionally also stub any shell wall whose segment the Pip→camera ray crosses (segment–segment test in xz), which covers corners. Then add the shell wall's `inside` meshes to the DR-12 ray test so a partially lowered wall also fades.
findings.verify: Re-run mockups/review5/tools/snap-grab-target/s8-meetwall.mjs and s9-sweeps.mjs m/s: expect `shell scales` ≈0.01 for the back wall at yaw+180, `pip:ok` and `pad:ok` on all 8 yaws at zoom 9, and retake snap-grab-target-60-mt-spawn-z9-y180 / s-pad-z9-y180 showing Pip.
findings.verify_reason: I reproduced it. In Meeting at spawn with zoom 9 and yaw .14+π, the camera settles at (-10.86,3.67,-12.03), 2.03 m outside the back-wall plane. Measured from the wall centre (0,-10), the cutaway test gives normal·toCam = 0.183, which is below the 0.2 threshold, so the back wall stays at scale 1. The frame is a blank wall and Pip and the plug are not visible. The geometry error at src/game.ts:385 is exactly as described.

findings.fix_correction: The fix is right. The test only needs the signed plane distance `wall.normal.dot(cam.position - wallOrigin) > 0.3`. Both 'at' and the normal are already in world space, and the lateral offset falls out. Keep the lerp-to-stub behaviour.

findings.title: Letting go of the plug (Q) right against the socket never seats it; the plug lies in the ring, unplugged, and the prompt moves on to the switch
findings.problem: The forgiving snap only runs inside interact() when F is pressed (src/game.ts:205). releasePlug() (src/game.ts:259-265), the Q path and the 'F Drop the plug' path outside range, never checks the socket. In Playground I held the plug facing the socket and pressed Q with the plug end 0.46 m from the socket centre. The prompt had just said 'F Plug in' (in range). The plug dropped visibly inside the cyan target ring, touching the socket box, and stayed `connected:false, electrical:off`. The same happened in Meeting at the power strip. A player who sees the plug lying in the ring believes it is in. The lamp then stays dark, and the next prompt reads 'E Switch on (needs power first)', which suggests the order is wrong rather than the plug. Hard rule 7 says a plug that looks in snaps in. Q is also the key the game advertises for 'let go', so releasing at the socket is a natural action.
evidence: s2 log: q03 plug->socket 0.46, after KeyQ connected false electrical off
findings.fix: Extract the seat test into `trySeat()` (the same condition as :205: `Math.min(dist(Pip,target)-.6, dist(plug,target))<1.6 && strain<1.12`) and call it at the top of releasePlug() when energy<=1, i.e. no slingshot, so chaos throws still fling. Also, in step(), a plug lying idle within 0.6 m of level.target for 0.3 s seats itself with the plugFlash. Use the same rule for the Lunch cable release (src/lunch-runtime.ts release()) and for the strip/robot/pod drops on Q (throw) when the item lands inside the snap radius.
findings.verify: New spec in tests/routes.spec.ts: 'a plug let go beside the socket seats': F, route to (5.95,-6), Q, wait .4 → expect connected (snapshot().electrical after the switch = on). Retake snap-grab-target-08 showing the plug flash.
findings.verify_reason: I reproduced it in Playground. The prompt read 'F Plug in', the plug was 0.46 m from the socket centre, and I pressed Q. Afterwards connected=false and electrical=off, and the plug lies inside the cyan ring touching the socket box. releasePlug() (src/game.ts:259-265) never runs a seat test.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/shots/verify-gap7-snap-grab-target-03-pg-afterQ.jpg (plug against socket box inside ring, not seated)
v1.mjs p log: beforeQ prompt 'FPlug in' plug->socket 0.46; afterQ connected false electrical off
findings.fix_correction: Run the seat test before calling this.rope.release(). release() returns the slingshot energy and resets the strain, so read rope.strain and evaluate the condition first. Seat only when energy<=1, so the slingshot chaos path is unchanged.

findings.title: No pre-release snap signpost at any cable socket: the target ring looks identical whether or not you hold the plug or are in range
findings.room: playground, meeting (also garage stand, spectrum pad/marks, lunch cap dock)
findings.problem: The only world cue at the Playground and Meeting sockets is the cyan torus built at src/game.ts:87. It pulses the same way all the time (src/game.ts:431, scale from this.time only). It doesn't react to holding the plug, to entering the 1.6 m snap zone, or to strain. At 1.5 m and 0.6 m with the plug in hand, the frames show the same ring as before pickup. There is no ghost plug, magnet line, colour change or brighter ring. The only change is the text pill 'F Plug in'. The power strip drop zone (2.6 m, game.ts:211) has no floor mark at all before release: the strip just appears at (t.x,.08,t.z+.3) afterwards. The garage test stand, the spectrum store pad (a ring that only shows which pad is current) and the Lunch capacitor dock (2 m, lunch-runtime.ts:232, no cue while pushing the cart) are the same. Lunch cable ports do brighten every ring to .95 while a cable is held (lunch-runtime.ts:311-312), which is the right idea but highlights every port, not the one that will take the plug. DR-14 asks for a cue from about 2 m out, and AGENTS 2 asks for icons and rings over text.
evidence: mockups/review5/shots/snap-grab-target-51-lu-cap-2m.jpg (cart 1.28 m from winch, inside dock radius, no cue, prompt still 'Push')
findings.fix: In Game.render: when holdingPlug, set the target ring to job yellow #ffd84a, opacity 1, and scale 1.3 once inside 3 m. Inside the snap condition, show a ghost plug (clone of this.plug, MeshBasic #ffd84a at opacity .45, depthTest:false, renderOrder 11) seated at (target.x,.28,target.z), plus a short dashed tether from the plug to the ghost, and play a soft 'click-ready' tick once on entering. For the strip: a dashed floor outline (0.9×0.35 m) at the snap pose while the strip is held within 4 m, solid yellow inside 2.6 m. Garage/Spectrum: reuse the same ghost helper with the robot/pod footprint at STAND/PADS. Lunch: brighten only the port the sort picks (scale 1.3, yellow), others stay at .35; for the cap dock, draw a ring at (12,-4.8) r=2 while the cart is held. Put the helper in src/render (e.g. snapGhost.ts) so every dock uses it.
findings.verify: Retake snap-grab-target-03/04/11/12/16/17/31/51: a yellow ghost or ring is visible at 1.5 m and brighter at 0.6 m; add an objectives.spec.ts check that the target ring colour changes when holdingPlug and in range.
findings.verify_reason: The code agrees. The torus pulses from this.time only (src/game.ts:431, `this.target.scale.setScalar(1+Math.sin(this.time*3)*.12)`) and ignores holdingPlug and range. Lunch rings switch to opacity .95 for every port whenever a cable is held (src/lunch-runtime.ts:311-312). The pre-pickup and in-range frames look the same apart from the text pill.

findings.title: Lunch picks the port nearest Pip's body, not the plug in his hand: holding the thick plug against the kitchen post plugs it into the fridge
findings.problem: In both interact() and promptAt(), the Lunch snap candidates are sorted by `distance(pos,p.pos)` with pos = Pip (src/lunch-runtime.ts:150-151 and :185). The kitchen feed post (-4,-3) and the fridge inlet (-4,-1.8) are only 1.2 m apart (lunch-runtime.ts:50-51), and the clean route comes in from the fridge side. I stood at (-3.29,-2.21) with the thick plug end pushed up against the post. The marker bounced over the post, the card said 'Power the kitchen's feed post', and the prompt said 'F Plug into the fridge'. F plugged the 10-bar thick cable into the fridge, so the oven and lamps stayed off. The prompt is honest, but the player is aiming with the plug, which is what they see. The result reads as 'it went in the wrong hole'. It also wastes the thick cable in a room where cable rating is taught.
evidence: mockups/review5/shots/snap-grab-target-21-lu-between-ports.jpg (plug at post, prompt 'Plug into the fridge')
s4 log: after F cables thick:b>fridge, oven:off fridge:on
findings.fix: Sort the candidates by distance from the held end, `g.handPosition()` / cable.ends[end], not by Pip (both :151 and :185), and break ties in favour of the port that the current step's at() points to (export a `stepTarget()` from objectives.ts). Highlight only the chosen port's ring (see the snap-signpost finding) so the choice is visible before F.
findings.verify: Re-run mockups/review5/tools/snap-grab-target/s4-lunch.mjs: at (-3.29,-2.21) the prompt reads 'Plug into the kitchen feed post' and after F the thick cable ports are b>kitchen; tests/lunch.spec.ts still passes.
findings.verify_reason: I reproduced the symptom at Pip (-3.29,-2.21): the prompt said 'Plug into the fridge' and F gave thick:b>fridge with the oven off. The stated cause is wrong, though. The held end (handPosition) was at (-3.87,-2.03), 0.26 m from the fridge port (-4,-1.8) and 0.98 m from the kitchen post (-4,-3). So the plug really was at the fridge port, not 'pushed against the post'. Sorting by hand distance, the proposed fix, would pick the fridge as well. The real problem is the layout: the fridge's logical inlet (-4,-1.8) is about 1.1–1.3 m in front of the fridge body at (-5.6,-2.3) (src/lunch-runtime.ts:80-82), on open floor right in front of the yellow post. From the default camera, a plug at the fridge port looks as if it is touching the post. The sort-by-Pip code at :151/:185 is still a latent mismatch.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/shots/verify-gap7-snap-grab-target-04-lu-between.jpg (hand visually at the yellow post, prompt 'Plug into the fridge')
v1.mjs l log: hand [-3.87,-2.03] pip [-3.29,-2.21]; afterF thick:b>fridge, oven:off fridge:on
src/lunch-runtime.ts:51 fridge port (-4,-1.8) vs fridge body src/lunch-runtime.ts:80,82 at (-5.6,-2.3)
findings.fix_correction: Move the fridge port onto its visible socket plate, about (-5.05,-2.6), so it is at least 1.8 m from the kitchen post. Or highlight only the port that will be chosen (yellow, scale 1.3) while a cable is held. Changing the sort key to handPosition alone does not change the outcome in this repro, though doing it for consistency is fine.

findings.title: Grab cue and prompt name different objects when junk is nearer than the floor plug: prompt says 'F Pick up the plug', the reticle brackets the mug, and E takes the mug
findings.problem: The job-item bias in reach() (src/game.ts:193, −2 m for any spec.id prop) works for props. With a mug 0.25 m nearer than the Meeting power strip, the prompt and reticle stay on the strip. But the reel plug is not a Prop, so it gets no bias. In interact(), E grabs the nearest prop whenever `reach(nearest) < distance(plug)` (src/game.ts:218). The reticle uses the same unbiased test (src/game.ts:434-435). promptFor() checks the plug before props (src/ui/objectives.ts:90). The result at the Playground start, with a mug 0.37 m away against the plug at 0.44 m: the prompt reads 'F Pick up the plug', the yellow floor brackets sit on the mug at (-7.16,4.72), and E picks up the mug ('Put the mug down'). After a Meeting Q-drop near the placed strip, the prompt says 'F Pick up the plug' while the reticle brackets the strip, and E lifts the strip off its spot, which un-powers the circuit. Three signals (card, prompt, cue) point at different things, against DR-18 and DR-42. It shows up exactly where clutter collects: around the reel and around the drop point.
evidence: src/game.ts:218 (plug pickup loses to any nearer prop on E)
s1 log: junk placed → prompt 'F Pick up the plug', reticle [-7.16,4.72] (mug), after E held 'mug'
s3 log: after Q prompt 'F Pick up the plug', reticle [12.3,-1.95] (placed strip)
s3 log: mug placed nearer than strip → prompt/reticle stay on strip (bias works for props)
findings.fix: Add one `grabTarget(pos,key)` in game.ts that returns {kind:'plug'|'prop'|..., at} and is used by interact(), the reticle (:433-436) and promptFor(), so all three always agree. Treat the plug as a job item: compare `this.reach(pos,nearest) < distance(pos,this.plugPosition)-2` (the same −2 as reach()). Exclude placed, Fixed job items (a stripPlaced() strip, a parked pod/robot) from nearest() unless no other target is in reach, so E at the door never lifts the placed strip by accident. When E and F would act on different objects, draw the reticle on the F target with a small plug glyph.
findings.verify: Re-run s1-pg.mjs (junk mug case): the prompt and reticle both on the plug, and E picks up the plug (holdingPlug true). s3-meet.mjs after Q: the reticle on the plug, not the strip. Add an objectives.spec.ts case that teleports a mug 0.3 m from Pip at spawn and expects the reticle position == plugPosition.
findings.verify_reason: I reproduced it with a mug 0.37 m away and the plug 0.44 m away. The prompt reads 'F Pick up the plug' and the reticle sits on the mug at (-7.16,4.72). The claim overstates the effect, though. The prompted key F (cableOnly) skips nearest() and does pick up the plug (holdingPlug true in my run), and the reticle is documented as 'what E would grab' (src/game.ts:432). So only the reticle and prompt disagree. Pressing the shown key works. In Meeting, E lifting the placed strip follows from the code (the strip has an id with a −2 bias, and src/game.ts:220 makes it Dynamic on grab), but I did not rerun that case. This is clarity polish, not a noticeable fun or play blocker.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/shots/verify-gap7-snap-grab-target-02-pg-junk.jpg
v1.mjs p log: junk prompt 'FPick up the plug' reticle [-7.16,4.72] nearest mug d .37; after F holdingPlug true
findings.fix_correction: Draw the reticle on whatever the prompt's key acts on: when the prompt is the F plug pickup, mark plugPosition. Separately, keep a placed (Fixed) strip out of nearest() so E at the door cannot unpower the circuit by accident.

findings.title: At the mail cart the reticle marks the second reel while the prompt says 'Attach the coupler first', and the floor-level reticle is hidden under the cart
findings.problem: The cart carries both parts: the coupler at (-3.6,4.7) and the extension reel at (-3,4.7). attachNear() correctly sorts the coupler first (src/game.ts:228). But the reticle picks `props.find(...)` (src/game.ts:433), the first match in array order, which is the extension reel, and promptFor() uses the same unsorted find (src/ui/objectives.ts:84). Standing at the spec spot with the plug in hand, the reticle sat on the reel at (-3,4.7) while the text said 'Attach the coupler first'. That makes the hidden coupler-before-reel rule (R4B M8) harder to read, because the cue points at the wrong-order part. The reticle is also drawn at floor height (y .03, game.ts:436), under the cart's deck, so in the screenshot the cue can't be seen at all. Both parts sit 0.74–0.97 m up on the cart.
evidence: mockups/review5/shots/snap-grab-target-15-mt-cart-attach-cue.jpg (no visible brackets; prompt 'Attach the coupler first')
s3 log: at cart reticle [-3,4.7] (extension) while prompt 'F Attach the coupler first'
findings.fix: Use attachNear's sorted selection (factor out `attachCandidate(pos)`) for the reticle and the prompt. Place the reticle at the target's bounding-box bottom (mesh.position.y − size[1]/2 + .02), or float it at the top of the part when it rests on another prop, and set depthTest:false, renderOrder 10 so it reads through the cart deck.
findings.verify: Re-run s3-meet.mjs: at (-3.57,5.46) the reticle equals the coupler position (-3.6,4.7) and is visible in a retaken snap-grab-target-15.
findings.verify_reason: Props are ordered with the extension before the coupler (src/levels/meeting.ts:27), so both the reticle find at src/game.ts:433 and the prompt find at src/ui/objectives.ts:84 return the extension. It is actually worse than reported. Because the find returns the extension and coupler=false, the prompt reads 'Attach the coupler first', yet F at that spot runs attachNear, which picks the coupler first and attaches it. The prompt therefore tells the player the wrong thing. The reticle sits at y .03 under the cart deck and cannot be seen in the shot.
extra_evidence: src/levels/meeting.ts:27 (extension pushed before coupler)
mockups/review5/shots/snap-grab-target-15-mt-cart-attach-cue.jpg checked: no visible reticle, prompt 'Attach the coupler first' while F would attach the coupler

findings.title: A plug dropped near the lamp switch is hidden behind the switch prompt: the card and marker say 'pick up the plug', the pill says 'E Switch on (needs power first)'
findings.problem: After the plug falls short within 1.9 m of switchAt, the step-2 marker hops onto the plug (objectives.ts step 2 at() = plugPosition), and the reticle brackets it. But promptFor() checks nearSwitch() before the plug (src/ui/objectives.ts:88 before :89), and interact() does the same (src/game.ts:216 before :218). So the pill offers 'E Switch on (needs power first)', and E clicks the switch instead of recovering the plug. Only F (never shown) picks the plug up. Right after a failed plug-in, the one prompt the player reads tells them to do something else.
evidence: s1/s2 logs: after Q prompt 'ESwitch on (needs power first)', reticle on plug
findings.fix: In promptFor(), when the plug is not connected and within 1.75 m, return 'F Pick up the plug' before the switch branch. Keep the switch prompt only when connected (it is useless before). Mirror this ordering in interact() for E (or let E also pick up the plug when it is the current step's target).
findings.verify: Re-run s2-pgdrop.mjs: after Q the pill reads 'F Pick up the plug'.
findings.verify_reason: I reproduced it. After Q, with the plug resting 0.46 m from the socket, the prompt reads 'E Switch on (needs power first)' and the step marker sits on the plug. Pressing E toggled the switch ('Switch it off' afterwards, still not connected) and did not recover the plug. The ordering is as cited at src/ui/objectives.ts:80-81 (nearSwitch before the plug) and src/game.ts:216-218.

findings.title: Garage pickup prompt calls the delivery robot 'the cart'
findings.problem: The robot is a `cart` prop with a robot mesh. Next to it, the generic prompt says 'E Grab the cart' (NAMES.cart in src/ui/objectives.ts:58, used at :92), while the card says 'Carry the delivery robot onto the test stand' (src/stations/garage/station.ts:97). Charging bay carts stand right beside it, so 'the cart' sends the player's eye to the wrong object at the moment of pickup, and the two texts break DR-50's one-name rule.

findings.title: Capacitor-cart dock prompt lags the real dock zone: 'Push the capacitor cart' shows while the cart is already inside the 2 m dock, and nothing in the world marks the dock
findings.problem: Docking tests the cart's position, `distance(capPos,{x:12,z:-4.8})<2` (src/lunch-runtime.ts:232). The prompt tests Pip's position, `distance(pos,{x:12,z:-4.8})<2.2` (lunch-runtime.ts:182). Pushing the cart ahead, it was 1.28 m from the winch (well inside the dock) while Pip was at 2.56 m, and the pill still said 'E Push the capacitor cart'. Releasing there docked it. The lift's port ring is the dim 0.35 one (it only brightens while a cable is held) and is hidden behind the cart. So the player can't tell when to let go, and may push the cart into the winch or keep shoving. Only after release does the cart lead appear (shot 52).
evidence: s7 log: ~2.2 capToWinch 1.28 pipToWinch 2.56 prompt 'Push the capacitor cart'; after E docked true
findings.fix: Use the cart position in the prompt test (`distance(capacitor.body.translation(),LIFT)<2` → 'Park the cart by the winch'), and while the cart is held, draw the dock ring (r 2 m, dashed, job yellow) and a ghost of the cart lead to the winch socket.
findings.verify: Re-run s7-lunchcap.mjs: at capToWinch < 2 the prompt reads the park text and a ring is visible in a retaken snap-grab-target-51.
findings.verify_reason: The code agrees. The prompt uses Pip's distance to (12,-4.8) <2.2 (src/lunch-runtime.ts:182), while docking uses the cart's distance <2 and requires that the cart not be held (src/lunch-runtime.ts:232). While pushing, the cart is ahead of Pip, so it enters the dock radius before the text changes. No dock ring is drawn for the cart. I did not rerun the push myself. The numbers come from the reviewer's log and agree with the code.
extra_evidence: src/lunch-runtime.ts:232 docked requires g.held!==capacitor, so the player must let go inside the zone without any cue

findings.title: The objective marker is a depth-tested cone at a fixed 2.1 m with no draw-through or off-screen arrow: it leaves the frame at zoom 9 and dips below 2–3 m walls
findings.room: all (playground, meeting, lunch, garage, spectrum checked)
findings.problem: The marker material (src/ui/objectives.ts:97) is a default MeshBasicMaterial (depthTest on, no renderOrder), positioned at y 2.1 ± 0.18 (objectives.ts:116). In the 8-yaw sweeps at each step's at() point: at zoom 9 it is outside the frame at 1–4 of 8 yaws even when the target itself is on screen (Playground step 2: marker OFF at y0–y180 with the socket visible at y180; Meeting step 1 at y180/y315). Behind the 2.1 m brick storeroom walls and 3 m shell walls it is occluded (Spectrum pad z9 y135/y180: marker HID). In the Playground it hides inside the 0.34 m lamp shade at zoom 38 (y135–y225). When the target is behind a non-Pip occluder, the occluder doesn't fade either (Spectrum pad HID by an op1 occluder at z9/z38 y0; Meeting reel plug HID by op1 occluders at z9 y225/270). So DR-13's escape hatch, 'the marker draws over', never applies. This is distinct from the already-filed 'no off-screen indicator' and 'pale cone' items: it is about depth and height.
evidence: mockups/review5/shots/snap-grab-target-sp-pad-z9-y0.jpg (pad behind brick wall at full opacity; marker grazing the HUD card)

findings.title: The job-item reach bias favours every id'd prop, not the current step's item: pins, bridges, splitters and the second reel all outrank the next thing the card asks for
findings.problem: reach() subtracts 2 m for any prop with a spec.id (src/game.ts:193). Ids are given to job items and also to decoration-like or later-step items: the six bowling pins ('pin-*'), Lunch's three bridges and three splitters, the Meeting extension reel. So with two id'd items in reach, plain distance decides again. At the mail cart, stepping 0.3 m toward the extension grabs the reel instead of the coupler, which leads straight into the hidden-order wobble. Near the pins, a pin beats a nearby required item, and a pin beats the bare floor plug (which has no bias at all, see the reticle finding). DR-18 says 'prefers the job item'. The code's own comment says 'Job items ... always win over clutter', but it can't tell the step's item from other ids.
evidence: s3 log: at cart both coupler and extension within 0.3 m of each other; nearest coupler d .76 vs extension .95 — order decided by distance only
findings.fix: Make the bias two-tier: −2 m for the item named by the current step's at() (export `currentTarget(g)` from objectives.ts: prop id or 'plug'), −0.5 m for other id'd items, 0 for clutter. Mark pins with a `bonus` flag that gets no bias.
findings.verify: Script: stand 0.3 m nearer the extension than the coupler at the mail cart without the coupler attached; E should pick up the coupler (snapshot().held==='coupler').
findings.verify_reason: reach() subtracts 2 m for any spec.id (src/game.ts:193), and ids exist on bowling pins (src/levels/playground.ts:18, not :17) and on both cart parts (src/levels/meeting.ts:27). With two id'd items in range, raw distance decides. The impact is minor. With the plug in hand, attachNear sorts the coupler first anyway, and F (cableOnly) always picks the plug over pins. So only the E grab ordering is affected, and picking up the extension early has no failure state: it just drops.

notes.playability: Snap and grab mostly work in code, but are signposted only in text. What works: the F snap is generous (Pip within 2.2 m or the plug within 1.6 m), the Meeting strip snaps from 2.6 m (M10 confirmed), the garage stand (2.6 m) and the spectrum pad and mirror marks (Pip within 2.2/2.1 m) agree with their prompts, and the Lunch capacitor docks inline (LR9 confirmed). The reach bias for id'd props works: a mug 0.25 m nearer than the power strip doesn't steal the prompt or the reticle. The gaps all sit on the release side. The Q/let-go path never seats a plug that lies in the socket ring. The Lunch port choice uses Pip's body, not the plug in his hand. The bare reel plug gets no job bias, so the reticle and E go to a nearer mug while the pill says F plug. The biggest camera problem is a geometry bug in the shell-wall cutaway (wall centre used instead of the wall plane): at the Meeting spawn and the Spectrum storeroom, a 180° orbit fills the screen with a wall and hides Pip, the item and the target.
notes.clarity: The prompt is honest about what F/E will do, but it is the only cue. The socket torus pulses the same way with or without the plug. There is no ghost, magnet or in-range colour change at any dock, and the strip, stand, pad and cart docks have no pre-release footprint at all. Lunch alone brightens its port rings while a cable is held, which is the right idea, but all of them light. The reticle, prompt and marker disagree in three repeatable cases: the junk-near-plug start, the mail cart (reticle on the reel, text says coupler) and a plug dropped near the lamp switch (pill offers the switch). The garage pickup calls the robot 'the cart'.
notes.teaching: Not the focus of this gap pass, but snapping affects the cable lesson. In Lunch, a thick cable meant for the feed post ends up in the fridge 1.2 m away, which muddles the rating/budget idea the room teaches. In Playground, a plug that looks seated but isn't makes the 'needs power first' switch prompt read as an order rule rather than a bad connection.
notes.fun: Forgiving snaps are what keep a Good Job-style game from feeling finicky. Here the clean action (walk up, F) feels fine, but the natural slapstick action (let the plug go at the socket) silently fails, and the camera can lose Pip completely in two starting corners. Fixing the release seat and the cutaway removes the two most frustrating moments seen in this pass.
notes.models: Not assessed in depth. Incidental: the floor-level grab reticle disappears under carts and stands (mail cart), the spectrum pod is carried at head height over Pip's face (sp-pad shots), and the garage robot could end up tipped on its side behind Pip after a backward approach (shot 33; not reproduced in a normal turnaround, s6).
